query: Why do some Amazon products receive predominantly negative reviews, and which factors contribute the most?

per_column.name: negative_theme_product_defect
per_column.rationale: A candidate substantive cause of negative sentiment; a real-world attribute (product defect) whose presence could drive the outcome.

per_column.name: negative_theme_poor_quality
per_column.rationale: Candidate cause of negativity reflecting product quality; plausibly drives the outcome.

per_column.name: negative_theme_misleading
per_column.rationale: Candidate cause: misleading listings could cause negative reviews.

per_column.name: negative_theme_shipping_issues
per_column.rationale: Candidate cause: shipping problems driving negativity.

per_column.name: negative_theme_customer_service
per_column.rationale: Candidate cause: service failures driving negativity.

per_column.name: negative_theme_disappointment
per_column.rationale: Disappointment is an emotional state on the causal path between a substantive problem and the expressed negative label; it is an outcome/mediator of dissatisfaction rather than an independent cause.

per_column.name: negative_theme_pricing
per_column.rationale: Candidate cause: pricing complaints driving negativity.

per_column.name: negative_theme_count
per_column.rationale: An aggregate count of the theme flags; it is a downstream summary of the themes and effectively co-determined with the label rather than a common cause of the individual treatments and the outcome.

per_column.name: negative_intensity_score
per_column.rationale: Intensity of negative language is a proxy/measure of the outcome itself (sentiment), on the causal path, not an independent confounder.

per_column.name: review_length_bucket
per_column.rationale: Review length can plausibly relate to the propensity to express/detect specific themes (treatment measurement) and to sentiment expression (outcome), making it a plausible common influence on both; the only column functioning as a genuine adjustment variable.

judge.rationale: The schema supplies multiple candidate treatments (thematic causes of negativity) so requirement (a) is met. However it largely fails requirement (b): the remaining added columns are mediators or proxies of the outcome (disappointment, negative_theme_count, negative_intensity_score) rather than common causes of both treatment and outcome. The only column plausibly acting as a surfaced confounder is review_length_bucket, but its status as a genuine common cause of a specific theme and sentiment is weak and more likely a measurement/detection artifact than a true confounder. No genuine background common causes (e.g., product category, price tier, brand, reviewer verification, expectation level) were surfaced, so the causal-attribution claim is only weakly realised.
